text: Nice that looks way better! Alright here is something else water related i came into the other day. So here is a prop i placed in some water, the prop is effectively a big ass rock (like haystack rock idea) [Image #1] ok and so if i go out to the rock and jump, and collide with it, i do collide into the prop and it has obvious physics rects./ However any of  the rock t hat is under water, seems to completely eliminate this physics rect and therefore i can walk through the prop [Image #2][Image #3][Image #4][Image #5]
resolution: Fixed the submerged-prop pass-through at the shared Zig physics boundary. collideSolidRects carried a legacy absolute-world guard (player head below Y=0 skipped every side collider), so the huge rock's oriented collider worked above sea level but vanished for a capsule fully on the -2.5m seabed. Collision now tests only capsule versus collider floor/top bands for both AABB and oriented rects; walk-under and top-clearance behavior stay unchanged. Added exact negative-elevation regressions for both paths and both pass. The ReleaseFast editor build and headless playtest smoke pass. A 60-second fixed-versus-legacy live gate over 573 rect plus 127 oriented colliders showed unchanged p99 (about 14.9ms) and no new tail; the full test-game-physics target retains one clean-HEAD ramp-speed assertion failure unrelated to this change.
